findings.explanation: The producer domain names input was validated only for a trailing dot, so a list of two or more domains passed validation and plan; the provider documents 'Current max number of domain names supported is 1' but does not enforce it in schema, so the API rejects it at apply. Principle is a best fit: this is an apply-time correctness bug.
findings.remediation: Validate that at most one domain is given.
findings.title: Service attachment domain_names accepts several domains but GCP supports only one

findings.explanation: Both addresses are created with count driven by whether var.consumer / var.google_apis is set, and both carry a hard-coded lifecycle.prevent_destroy. Setting either input back to null, changing var.name (ForceNew on the address name), or removing the module call fails plan with 'Instance cannot be destroyed', and a caller of the published module cannot override lifecycle, so the only way out is state surgery. The Google APIs address is always pinned to var.google_apis.ip_address, so a replacement would keep its IP anyway; only an auto-allocated consumer IP is at risk.
findings.remediation: Decide whether IP stability or the optional-part interface wins: drop prevent_destroy (and recommend pinning consumer.ip_address), or keep it and document that the parts are one-way once created.
findings.title: prevent_destroy on count-toggled PSC addresses makes the consumer and Google APIs parts impossible to disable or rename
